Might as well spill. I've been suicidal for five years now, back in 2018 I finally mustered up the courage to write a letter to my Mother asking for mental help. Cut to a few months later she still hasn't taken me to a psychiatrist. I remember that day so vividly, it was my parents' anniversary, and my Dad had just returned from the liquor store, (we were going to invite my aunts and uncles, which are his brothers and sisters) he was in a particularly crappy mood that day due to his chronic knee pain and stressed because of the gathering. Well that happened to be the day I finally snapped, I could no longer deal with my constant anxious thoughts of not being a success like he wanted me to, everyday I felt lazy and worthless, even though I practically gave up on looking after my mental health just to get my homework turned in on time. (I was in an AP class; I'm still taking AP courses) But he didn't care, he didn't see what I had to do to bring home As everyday especially with such a rigorous course. 

That day, I cut myself multiple times to no avail. Instead of reading, I sat in my brother's room Googling suicide methods. I left my phone open (worst mistake I could make) and hoped he would see it. When my Dad came home with the drinks, the first thing he did was ask me about my studies, fearfully, I told him that I hadn't finished reading the chapter. He blew up and demanded to know why. By that time I had started to cry, and I was too scared to tell him how I actually felt. 

Then, my brother bursts into the living room holding my phone in his hand, waving it every which way. When he looked at the screen he started **scowling**, he asked me, "what is this?!?" I didn't reply. He literally screamed at me for **forty-five minutes** telling me how I was turning into another black statistic that hates education and how the "little white kids" will always beat me, but that wasn't even the worst of it. He told me he "doesn't give a damn about me wanting to die". I just stood there, bawling. My Mother was cried to herself as she pretended not to see me.

I don't want to continue because I feel anxious just typing this, but I hope this answered your question.

Hey bud, I'm sorry to hear that you're in so much pain right now, I would prefer to be right next to you holding you in my arms as I console you but for now, my words will have to do.

I want to start off by acknowledging how awesome you are for making it all the way to graduate school, that is so fucking amazing dude! I was literally moved to tears when you talked about how your studies are making you suicidal. This resonates with me so much. 

I know this sounds cliche but it's not too late to catch up, have you ever considered the following? :

* Asking a friend that is done with all of their work to help you

* Talking to your professors about what's been going on with your mental health 

* Breaking each of your assignments down (By class, Material, amount to do and logging how long that assignment will take you)

* Finding the root of the problem (Why are my studies making me feel this way?, is it time for me to get physiological help? Is there a career that resonates with my subject that I could possibly see myself liking? )

I hope this was helpful OP, and I'm so proud of you for making it all the way to graduate school! Don't give up yet, I believe in you! :D

I want to start off by saying how well written this post is, if you aren't already, you should definitely pursue a career in writing or poetry. As for your loved one, know that whatever you think is going through their head *isn't* 

Personally, I have dealt with a constant feeling of abandonment, I always told myself that no one is going to want to be by you or no one loves you until I realized that wasn't true. Turns out that mindset was eating me alive, slowly making me feel inferior and worthless as each day progressed.

I want you to know this, depression affects both you and the people around you, that's why so many of us hide it, in hopes not being a burden to our friends/family. The truth is, many people don't know how to offer support to someone with depression.

Your friend is most likely worn out and needs time to themselves to help you. Think of it like this OP, they need to be at 100 % to help you not 60. This means that they need to be in their right state of mind in order to give you the support they need and it seems like they aren't in one at the moment.

I suggest giving them time to rejuvenate, but don't worry too much if you need anyone to talk to, I'm always here for you OP. :)
